descriptionChirho: A Greek unit of linear measurement equal to approximately 185 meters or 607 feet (στάδιον as measure), used in the NT to express distances traveled or between locations (John 6:19, 11:18; Luke 24:13; Revelation 14:20, 21:16). Multilingual evidence: Arabic مَسافَة (masāfa, 'distance')/غَلْوَة (ghalwa, 'furlong'), Korean 스타디온 (seutadion, transliteration), Swahili stadia (transliteration), Hindi स्टेडिया (sṭeḍiyā, transliteration), Spanish estadios. The plural and genitive forms simply express varying distances, not a different concept.

A physical arena or racecourse where athletic contests are held (στάδιον as structure/venue), used metaphorically by Paul in 1 Corinthians 9:24 comparing the Christian life to a foot-race in a stadium. Multilingual evidence clearly distinguishes this from the measurement sense: Arabic مَيْدان (maydān, 'arena/field'), Korean 경기장 (gyeonggijang, 'stadium/arena'), Swahili uwanja-wa-mbio ('field-of-running/racecourse'), Hindi दौड़-के-मैदान (dauṛ-ke-maidān, 'running-field'), Spanish estadio (here meaning the venue itself). The shift from abstract distance to concrete architectural place is consistent across all translations.
